name: The streaming box on the wall and the phone

artboards.title: Today: an Apple TV asleep, on the wall
A: its apps on the card
B: Watch opens a pane of its apps
C: the card is the last thing on

annotations.text:
WHY THIS EXISTS

The TV's own screen has a Watch row (design/tv-box/, A). The wall and the phone show the same Apple TV as a TV card that says Off with a power button, under a picture of a television: nothing about what was on or what it can play. Somebody on the sofa with only their phone, or passing the wall, can't start anything on the TV.

The brain already has what every direction needs: the box's apps, what the house has seen used, and what was last on when the box said so.

TODAY

The shipped panel on the pretend house at 8:10 PM with its TV asleep. Awake and playing, the card is tall, with the show, pause and how far through; that stays in every direction.

THE SAME IN EVERY DIRECTION

THE CARD STAYS ITS SIZE. Each board redraws only the TV card, in exactly its place, so the room's arrangement and its test don't move.

ITS OWN NAME. The card says Apple TV, as the household named it, not TV under a picture of one; asleep is Asleep, not Off.

OPENING AN APP FROM HERE: the box wakes and opens it, and switches the TV over itself, as an Apple TV does when it wakes. If it was already awake, the TV's screen sees it start and switches the TV.

PLAYING, the card is today's tall card, and tapping it opens the same choice of apps as asleep.

Apps by name on a quiet tint, never a logo, the used ones first, as on the TV.

A: ITS APPS ON THE CARD

Asleep, the card is the three apps the house uses most and More. One tap from the room starts one.

FOR: The fewest taps of the three.

AGAINST: Three buttons and a More on a card the size of a lamp's; on the phone only two fit. The card reads as a menu rather than a thing in the room, and it says nothing about what was on.

B: WATCH OPENS A PANE OF ITS APPS

Asleep, the card is calm, the way every card is: Apple TV, Asleep, what was last on when that is known, and one Watch button. Watch, or a tap anywhere on it, opens its pane: what was last on, then every app, laid out like the TV's own Watch row.

FOR: The card stays one thing with one button, and the pane is the same choice the TV's screen gives. It doesn't lean on knowing what was last on, which an Apple TV often doesn't say: without it the card still reads Asleep and Watch.

AGAINST: Two taps to start anything, even the show you always watch.

Try it: tap the card.

C: THE CARD IS THE LAST THING ON

Asleep, the card is what was on last, its picture behind the words, the way a speaker's card is its song (design/speaker-card/, A). Play starts it again; Other apps, or holding the card, opens B's pane.

FOR: The commonest thing, carrying on, is one tap, and the room looks like what it was doing.

AGAINST: It stands on knowing what was last on. Through Home Assistant an Apple TV said nothing at all for Netflix on 20 November, so on many evenings this card would be a guess or blank.

Try it: tap play, or Other apps.

RECOMMENDED: B

It is the only direction that reads right whatever the box reports, and the box reports less than we hoped: the apps are always known, what was last on often isn't. The card stays calm and the same size, and the pane is the TV's own Watch row in another shape, so a household learns one choice, not three.

From C, keep one thing: when what was last on is known, the pane leads with it, as drawn.

DECIDED 20 NOVEMBER 2026 -- B

Asleep, a streaming box's card says Asleep, what was last on when the house knows it, and Watch, in the TV card's own place. Watch opens its pane: what was last on, then seven apps, the used ones first, and All apps. A tap opens it on the box, which switches the TV over; where it was already awake, the TV's own screen does. Playing, the card is today's, and its pane has Something else.

A and C are kept on the page beside this one, with their cases.

NOT CHOSEN

A made the card a menu too small for its buttons. C stood on knowing what was last on, which an Apple TV often doesn't say. B reads right whatever the box reports.
